qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what combination of clinical findings led the team to defer repeat abdominal imaging despite the patient’s fear of obstruction?
qas.answer: Stable vitals, reassuring labs/exam, symptoms consistent with prior illness.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, why did the doctor say the gastroenteritis might last longer in this patient than in others?
qas.answer: Altered GI anatomy makes the gut more sensitive, slower to recover.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what was the rationale for holding G-tube feeds while prioritizing IV fluids and gradual oral intake?
qas.answer: Tube feeds could worsen diarrhea during acute gut inflammation.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, why did the team emphasize gabapentin and acetaminophen and minimize IV opioids like Dilaudid?
qas.answer: Opioids can slow gut motility and worsen nausea/abdominal discomfort.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, how did the doctor interpret the mildly elevated AST in the context of otherwise reassuring labs?
qas.answer: Likely dehydration/stress-related rather than major liver injury.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what reasoning supported not repeating stool studies (including norovirus and C. diff) early in the stay?
qas.answer: Recent same diagnosis, unchanged symptoms, prior C. diff negative, no new red flags.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, why was loperamide avoided, and what alternative strategy was used instead?
qas.answer: Previously worsened symptoms; used hydration and gentle diet/supportive care.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what symptom trend from 2174-10-27 through 2174-10-30 supported advancing diet and discharging the patient?
qas.answer: Vomiting stopped and diarrhea steadily improved while oral intake increased.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what discharge readiness criteria did the doctor specify, and how did the patient meet them by the final morning?
qas.answer: Tolerate fluids/food, nausea controlled orally, stable labs; patient eating/drinking with stable bloodwork.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, how did the doctor address the patient’s feeling of being “punished” for requesting pain medication?
qas.answer: Explained balancing pain control with gut recovery; promised frequent reassessment.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, why were antibiotics not prescribed even though symptoms were severe and prolonged?
qas.answer: Suspected norovirus; antibiotics don’t treat viral gastroenteritis.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2174-10-26 to 2174-10-30, what features of the G-tube site assessment supported continuing topical care rather than treating a deep infection?
qas.answer: Only serosanguinous crusting; no spreading redness, pus, fever.
